description: A sampler that records what is patched into it, then plays it back at any speed, forwards or backwards, between chosen start and end points

params.text: Starts recording on each press, clearing whatever was there; the next press stops it
Starts or stops playing on each press when ONE-SHOT is on; with it off, playing runs for as long as the button is held
Sets the playback speed, half at one end and one and a half times at the other, and the pitch with it
Reverses the direction of play on each press
Throws the recorded sample away on each press
Sets where playback begins, as a fraction of the recorded sample from its start to its end
Sets where playback ends, as a fraction of the recorded sample from its start to its end
Switches between stopping at the end point and running round from the end point back to the start
Switches between playing the sample once for each trigger, and playing it only while the play control is held

inputs.text: A rising edge starts recording, clearing whatever was there; the next stops it
A rising edge starts or stops playing when ONE-SHOT is on; with it off, playing runs for as long as this jack is above 0V
Adds to the playback speed; -5V stops it, 0V leaves the knob alone and 5V doubles what the knob gives
A rising edge reverses the direction of play
A rising edge throws the recorded sample away

outputs.text: The sample as it plays, or the incoming signal while recording

notes: nothing comes out until something has been recorded; the module ships empty and the sample is not saved with the patch.
the speed control is the average of the knob and the CV jack, so the knob alone spans half speed to one and a half times, and the jack is needed to reach a standstill or double speed.
playback reads whole samples with no smoothing between them, so a speed other than 1 is noticeably grainy.
the red lamp is lit while recording and the green lamp while playing.
an edge is counted only when a jack or button moves away from exactly 0V and no further edge is counted until it returns there.
with END set below START the two are pulled together and playback stays on one sample.
